tweets: A malicious contract can take over control flow by calling back before the first function invocation finishes.
This allows repeated use of stale state because external contracts may reenter before the initial call completes.
The root cause is that state updates often occur after an external call rather than before it.
Remediation requires performing all internal state changes before executing any external calls.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern for avoiding reentrancy weaknesses.
Using a reentrancy lock blocks unwanted callbacks into the protected path without preventing control passing to the callee.
